title: Playing as well as ever, practising daily and when he will quit
summary: He thinks he plays more securely than in the Condon days, practises an hour or more a day, and will quit if he slips.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: fortunately, I've had good health up to this point - my wife too and we've lugged some pretty heavy suitcases around; and travelling, you're lucky if you've got some money in your pocket - you can get your bags taken care of. And, that's what we have to do; I can't lift all those heavy things--

But, uh, up to this point, I would say that nothing has impaired my playing; I still feel the same and I play the same - even sometimes I feel that I play a little a more secure than I did back in the CondOn days - look, it's been 30 years since then - 30 something years -- in music, you learn something everyday of your life but even when you practice you say - oh, how did I do that; I must try that again. You know, or something.
And, that's still going on as far as you're concerned---
Well, as long as you've got your teeth and your health - there's no reason why you can't play.
But you do make a point of--- like, you haven't been playing while we've been doing all this taping each day - so you practice everyday--
Well, I have to. You know.
An hour - an hour and a half every-day.
When I was 20 years old, I didn't. But, then, the older you get the harder it is to soften up your lip and keep your lip going-- and I don't know how long
Well, you're going to play as long as you can play well-- that's your idea, isn't it?
Yeah. If I ever - within the next couple - three years or so, If I feel I'm slipping, I'll quit and I'm going to hang it up. It would be like JOe Lewis - quite while you're ahead.
